content.title: About
content.content: Bread with zucchini is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates grated zucchini into the dough. The vegetable adds moisture, a subtle flavor, and boosts the nutritional profile with vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Zucchini is one of the lowest‑calorie vegetables, containing over 90 % water.
Adding zucchini to dough improves crumb softness and aroma.
Bread with zucchini is traditional in Mediterranean cuisine, where the squash is used in many summer dishes.
Zucchini is rich in vitamin C, which partially degrades during baking but some remains.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Zucchini provides vitamin C, supporting the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: The added zucchini contributes soluble and insoluble fiber, aiding digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Because of its high water content, the loaf remains relatively low‑calorie compared with regular white bread.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in zucchini, such as lutein, have antioxidant effects.

items.title: Allergy to cucurbit vegetables
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to zucchini.

items.title: Glucosinolates content
items.content: Raw zucchini contains glucosinolates that can irritate the stomach in large amounts; baking destroys most of these compounds.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the bread is made with added salt, monitor intake, especially for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread with zucchini works well for breakfast, as a sandwich base, or alongside soups and salads. It can be toasted and topped with olive oil, avocado, or your favorite spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months.
